chunks: From him, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ritual bath on the Day of Arafah in the cities, so he said, 'Bathe wherever you are.'
ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim perform the Ghusl on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to Aban ibn Taghlib underscores the jurisprudential principle of ease (*taysir*) in Hajj rituals, confirming that the recommended bath for the Day of Arafah is not geographically bound to the sacred precincts. This ruling alleviates the burden on pilgrims who may be dispersed in various camps (*amsar*) rather than concentrated in Mina, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical flexibility within the framework of ritual purity.
